title: Boeuf Bourguignon
subtitle: Slow-braised beef in red wine with bacon and mushrooms
excerpt: Braising steak simmered for three hours in Burgundy wine with bacon lardons, pearl onions, button mushrooms, and a bouquet garni until the beef is completely tender and the sauce is glossy and dark.

recipe.sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is the defining dish of Burgundy, the wine-producing region of eastern France. It was popularised outside France by Julia Child's 'Mastering the Art of French Cooking' (1961), which gave the recipe to a generation of American and British home cooks. The dish is a braise: the beef is first browned, then submerged in wine and stock and cooked very slowly until the collagen in the tougher cuts breaks down to gelatine, creating a richly textured sauce. It improves overnight. Serve with crusty bread or mashed potato.

recipeTools.notes: A 28 cm oven-proof casserole dish or Dutch oven.

content.text: Brown the beef in small batches: overcrowding the pan will steam the meat rather than brown it, and the browned crust is where much of the flavour comes from. The wine must be one you would drink: it does not need to be expensive, but it must be drinkable. Cheap cooking wine will make the sauce bitter.
Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Pat the beef dry and season. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the lardons over medium heat until golden. Add the pearl onions and cook for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.

Return the beef. Pour in the wine and stock. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer to the oven. Cook for 2 hours 30 minutes to 3 hours until the beef is tender when pressed.
In the last 20 minutes, fry the mushrooms in a little oil in a separate pan until golden. Stir into the casserole for the final 15 minutes. Check the seasoning. Scatter with parsley and serve.
